title: ENGRAM Collective: memory contracts, durable handoffs and measured reuse

reliability_lab.method: Real production memory, graph and handoff functions invoked directly, without provider inference. Tasks are controlled infrastructure consumers, not autonomous agent completions.

writes.scope: Production memory/store operations, not autonomous agents or LLM throughput

reads.scope: Production memory/store operations, not autonomous agents or LLM throughput

live_series.protocol: Four sequential live pairs; alternating reuse-first / baseline-first, no discarded warmup, same model, files and ten-test acceptance. Known-correct artifact baseline, not code-generation avoidance. Memory capsules and preflight preparation are production behavior. Both arms disable automatic post-run curation. Timing includes queue/startup, provider waits and execution until completion; not container cleanup. Stop on failure, keep its receipts and unknown billed usage. No general cost/latency guarantee.
limitations: One workstation and provider account; small sample with shared warm services.
SDK-internal retries are not separately counted. Failed-call billed tokens may be unknown.

limitations: The load and recovery lab directly invokes real production functions. It makes zero provider calls and is not autonomous-agent reasoning or model throughput.
Four alternating live pairs are a small local sample. One latency pair was slower; no general latency or cost guarantee is made.
The exact four-pair measured runtime is preserved with its source digest. Later private-reference protection, procedure binding and coordinator context/scope recovery were hardened separately.
Context token counts describe memory projections, not the entire model request. Explicit full reads are separately accounted. Fingerprints are hashes, not cryptographic signatures.
Handoff delivery is idempotent within this application. Exactly-once external side effects and distributed SQL/graph transactions are not claimed.
Local CPU embeddings dominate semantic-write latency. The measured 16-write trial is not a FalkorDB performance benchmark.

The earlier Qwen-to-20B scenario required recovery. The extra mission retains unsuccessful 20B quota and 120B scope/budget attempts; it is not labeled as first-attempt success. Read its explicit current phase and passed flag.
Temporary public hosting depends on the laptop. Permanent hosting and publication of the matching source repository remain pending.
